The plan gives no guidance on whether to use `git -C .tickets-tracker config`, `git config --global`, or a step-level `working-directory` — the correct invocation context is non-obvious to an implementer
findings.finding: The plan says to set `merge.ours.driver=true` 'for the tickets worktree' but does not specify the git config scope or invocation context. In reconcile-bridge.yml the merge runs inside `.tickets-tracker` (a linked worktree). If the config is written with `git config` in the main checkout context (e.g. `git -C . config merge.ours.driver true`), it lands in the main `.git/config` which the linked worktree also reads via its shared git dir — so it would work incidentally. But if the implementer uses `git -C .tickets-tracker config --local`, it applies only to the worktree's local config (correct). If `--global` is used it affects all repos on the runner (overly broad but functional). The plan's silence on scope leaves a mechanism gap: an implementer who writes the config in the wrong place may silently not fix the bug.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — first AC bullet; 'Files' section; Why section
scenarios: Implementer adds `git config merge.ours.driver true` in the main checkout context instead of inside the tickets worktree context — silently works (shared git dir), but the intent is unclear and a worktree with a separate git dir would miss it
Implementer uses `git -C .tickets-tracker config --local merge.ours.driver true` — correct for this case but would fail if the worktree has a separate git dir in a different setup
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step immediately after 'Mount tickets branch as a worktree' using `git -C .tickets-tracker config merge.ours.driver true` (local to the worktree's shared git dir). Alternatively, since linked worktrees share the main repo's git dir, `git config merge.ours.driver true` in the main checkout context also works — but document which is intended.

findings.finding: AC2's sole verification criterion — 'no conflict markers' — is necessary but not sufficient to prove local-wins behaviour. A 3-way text merge of the 18 MB JSON file could theoretically complete without conflict markers (if the diverged chunks do not overlap) and the test would pass green even though the ours-driver shortcut never fired and remote content overwrote local state.
scenarios: Remote diverges in a section the local branch did not touch → text merge succeeds, no markers, but the ours driver was never invoked; test still passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit content-equality assertion in the integration test: after the merge, run `diff <(git show LOCAL_REF:.bridge_state/state.json) .bridge_state/state.json` and assert exit 0, proving the local version was kept intact rather than text-merged.
